accounts.auto-switch.risk: Off unless you turn it on. With it on, Branch may move work between your own account and the accounts you marked kept separate (someone else's, or work's): it picks the one with the most left and moves on when one reaches its plan limit. Only an account you mark kept separate (someone else's, or work's) may share work with yours.

channel-setup.r.imessage.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.imessage.noCreate: Messages has no bot to create: the assistant answers as you, on your own Mac.
channel-setup.r.imessage.step-1: Only on a Mac: sign in to Messages with your Apple Account.
channel-setup.r.imessage.step-2: Let Branch read Messages (System Settings, Privacy and Security, Full Disk Access) and control it (Automation).
channel-setup.r.instagram.how: Make a Meta app with Instagram messaging for your professional account, then copy its token and app secret.
channel-setup.r.instagram.noApp: Instagram has no desktop app to install; messages are handled through Meta's developer site.
channel-setup.r.instagram.noCheck: Meta's read-only check needs the token inside the address, which Branch never does.
channel-setup.r.instagram.paste-META_VER: A word of your own choosing, typed into Meta's webhook page too
channel-setup.r.irc.field-server: The network's server name, like irc.libera.chat
channel-setup.r.irc.noApp: IRC is an open protocol with many programs; Branch connects by itself, so nothing needs installing.
channel-setup.r.irc.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.irc.noCreate: IRC networks register nicks by chat command, not on a web page.
channel-setup.r.irc.step-1: Pick a network, for example Libera.Chat.
channel-setup.r.irc.step-2: Register the assistant's nick with the network (Libera.Chat: /msg NickServ REGISTER).
channel-setup.r.irc.step-3: Paste its password here if it has one.
channel-setup.r.keybase.field-path: The full path to the keybase program
channel-setup.r.keybase.noCheck: Nothing to paste: the keybase program holds the account.
channel-setup.r.keybase.noCreate: Keybase bots are ordinary accounts made in the Keybase app.
channel-setup.r.keybase.step-1: Install Keybase and sign in with the assistant's account.
channel-setup.r.keybase.step-2: Put the full path to the keybase program in the connections line.
channel-setup.r.kook.how: On KOOK's developer site, create an application, open Bot, choose WebSocket, and copy the token.
channel-setup.r.line.how: Make a Messaging API channel, then copy its channel access token and channel secret.
channel-setup.r.mastodon.field-server: Your Mastodon server, for example https://mastodon.social
channel-setup.r.mastodon.how: Your server opens its new-application page. Give it a name, keep read and write, save, and copy Your access token.
channel-setup.r.mastodon.noApp: Mastodon runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.
channel-setup.r.matrix.field-server: Your homeserver's address, for example https://matrix.org
channel-setup.r.matrix.how: Make a separate account for the assistant on your homeserver, sign in with it, and copy its access token from Settings, Help and About.
channel-setup.r.mattermost.field-server: The address of your own server, starting with https://
channel-setup.r.mattermost.how: In your Mattermost, open Integrations, add an incoming webhook for a channel and copy its address; add an outgoing webhook too if the assistant should answer.
channel-setup.r.mattermost.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.
channel-setup.r.messenger.how: Make a Meta app with the Messenger product, link your page, and copy the page access token and the app secret.
channel-setup.r.messenger.noApp: Messenger's desktop app has been retired; the page is managed on the web.
channel-setup.r.messenger.noCheck: Meta's read-only check needs the token inside the address, which Branch never does.
channel-setup.r.messenger.paste-META_VER: A word of your own choosing, typed into Meta's webhook page too
channel-setup.r.mqtt.noApp: MQTT is a message protocol, not an app; Branch connects to your broker by itself.
channel-setup.r.mqtt.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.mqtt.noCreate: A broker is yours to run; there is nothing to create on a web page.
channel-setup.r.mqtt.step-1: Use the MQTT broker you already run (for example Mosquitto).
channel-setup.r.mqtt.step-2: Make a user for the assistant and paste its password here.
channel-setup.r.msteams-bot.how: In the Teams Developer Portal, open Bot management, add a bot, make a client secret, and copy the bot id and the secret.
channel-setup.r.msteams.how: In the Teams channel, add an incoming webhook (Microsoft now suggests the Workflows app for this) and copy its address.
channel-setup.r.msteams.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.
channel-setup.r.mumble.noCheck: Mumble is tried by connecting to the server when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.mumble.noCreate: Mumble has no accounts to create; the assistant joins a server by name.
channel-setup.r.mumble.paste-MUMBLE_PASS: The server password, if there is one
channel-setup.r.mumble.step-1: Install Mumble to talk to the assistant.
channel-setup.r.mumble.step-2: Give Branch the server name and a username for the assistant.
channel-setup.r.nextcloud-talk.field-roo: The conversation token from the room's address
channel-setup.r.nextcloud-talk.how: Your Nextcloud opens on Security. Make an app password for the assistant's account and copy it.
channel-setup.r.nostr.noApp: Nostr is an open protocol with many programs; Branch connects by itself.
channel-setup.r.nostr.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.nostr.noCreate: Nostr keys are made by programs, not on a sign-up page.
channel-setup.r.nostr.step-1: Make a private key for the assistant in a Nostr program you trust, on this computer. Never make one on a website.
channel-setup.r.nostr.step-2: Paste the key (nsec or hex) here.
channel-setup.r.ntfy.noApp: ntfy needs no desktop program; the phone app shows the notifications.
channel-setup.r.ntfy.noCheck: A public topic has nothing to check; the first notification is the test.
channel-setup.r.ntfy.noCreate: ntfy needs no account: you choose a hard-to-guess topic name and subscribe to it in the phone app.
channel-setup.r.ntfy.paste-NTFY_ACCESS_T: An access token, only for a server that asks for one
channel-setup.r.ntfy.step-1: Choose a long, hard-to-guess topic name.
channel-setup.r.ntfy.step-2: Subscribe to it in the ntfy phone app.
channel-setup.r.pumble.how: Create a Pumble app for your workspace and copy its app key, bot token and signing secret.
channel-setup.r.pumble.noCheck: Pumble does not document a read-only check for a bot token.
channel-setup.r.pushover.how: Pushover opens its new-application page. Name it Branch, create it, and copy its API token. Your user key is on the Pushover home page.
channel-setup.r.pushover.noApp: Pushover's desktop client runs in the browser; the phone app shows the notifications.
channel-setup.r.qq-bot.how: Sign in to the QQ bot platform, create a bot, and copy its AppID and AppSecret.
channel-setup.r.reddit.how: Reddit opens its apps page. Create a script app and copy its id (under the name) and its secret.
channel-setup.r.reddit.noApp: Reddit runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.
channel-setup.r.reddit.noCheck: Reddit's check means signing in, which Branch does when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.revolt.how: In Settings, My Bots, create a bot and copy its token.
channel-setup.r.rocketchat.field-server: The address of your own server, starting with https://
channel-setup.r.rocketchat.how: In Administration, Integrations, make an incoming integration for a channel and copy its address; make an outgoing one with a token if the assistant should answer.
channel-setup.r.rocketchat.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.
channel-setup.r.signal.noCheck: Nothing to paste: signal-cli holds the account itself.
channel-setup.r.signal.noCreate: Signal has no bot API. Branch talks through signal-cli, a separate open-source program (not made by Signal) that you install yourself; Branch never installs it.
channel-setup.r.signal.step-1: Install signal-cli from its own releases page (github.com/AsamK/signal-cli).
channel-setup.r.signal.step-2: Link it to your phone's Signal as a new device, or register a second number with it.
channel-setup.r.signal.step-3: Put the full path to signal-cli and the number in the connections line.
channel-setup.r.simplex.noCheck: Nothing to paste: SimpleX has no tokens.
channel-setup.r.simplex.noCreate: SimpleX has no accounts to create; the assistant's address is made by simplex-chat.
channel-setup.r.simplex.step-1: Install SimpleX Chat on your phone and connect to the assistant's address once it runs.
channel-setup.r.simplex.step-2: Run simplex-chat (from SimpleX's own releases page) with its WebSocket port on this computer; Branch does not install it.
channel-setup.r.slack.how: Slack opens its new-app page with Branch's settings filled in. Pick your workspace and press Create, then Install. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token, and under Basic Information make an app-level token with connections:write.
channel-setup.r.slack.pairing: Send the app a direct message in Slack. It answers with a six-digit code; approve it under Customize, Chat apps.
channel-setup.r.slack.paste-SLACK_BOT_TO: The Bot User OAuth Token, starting xoxb-
channel-setup.r.sms.how: In the Twilio Console, copy the Account SID and Auth Token, and buy or pick a number.
channel-setup.r.sms.noApp: Twilio is a web service; nothing to install.
channel-setup.r.synology-chat.field-serv: The address of your own server, starting with https://
channel-setup.r.synology-chat.how: In Synology Chat, open Integration, make an incoming webhook and an outgoing webhook, and copy the address and the token.
channel-setup.r.synology-chat.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.
channel-setup.r.telegram.how: BotFather opens with /newbot already typed. Send it, then give the bot a name and a username ending in bot. BotFather answers with the token.
channel-setup.r.telegram.pairing: Send any message to your bot in Telegram. It answers with a six-digit code; type that code here.
channel-setup.r.telegram.paste-TELEGRAM_: The token BotFather sends: digits, a colon, then a long run of letters
channel-setup.r.threema.how: Sign up for Threema Gateway, request a Basic ID, and copy the ID and its secret.
channel-setup.r.threema.noCheck: Threema's check needs the secret inside the address, which Branch never does.
channel-setup.r.twist.field-conversation: The id of the conversation to answer in
channel-setup.r.twist.how: Make a Twist integration, or a test token from its OAuth section, and copy the access token.
channel-setup.r.twist.noCheck: Twist's read-only check was not confirmed in its documentation, so Branch does not guess one.
channel-setup.r.twitch.how: Register an application, then make a user access token for the bot's account with the chat:read and chat:edit scopes.
channel-setup.r.twitch.noApp: Twitch chat runs in the browser; Branch connects by itself.
channel-setup.r.twitch.paste-TWITCH_CHAT: The bot account's user access token
channel-setup.r.viber.how: Create a bot account through Viber's partner site and copy its token.
channel-setup.r.vk.how: In your community's settings, open API usage, create a token with messages access, and switch on the Long Poll API.
channel-setup.r.vk.noApp: VK runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.
channel-setup.r.webex.how: Sign in to Webex for Developers, create a bot and copy its access token.
channel-setup.r.webex.paste-WEBEX_WEBHOO: A secret of your own for the webhook
channel-setup.r.wechat-mp.how: In your verified Official Account's developer settings, copy the AppSecret, set a Token and EncodingAESKey, and choose safe mode.
channel-setup.r.wechat-mp.noCheck: WeChat only takes the AppSecret inside the address, which Branch never does, so it is checked on first connection.
channel-setup.r.wecom-app.how: In the WeCom admin console, make a self-built app, and copy its Secret; under Receive messages set a Token and EncodingAESKey.
channel-setup.r.wecom-app.noCheck: WeCom only takes the secret inside the address, which Branch never does, so it is checked on first connection.
channel-setup.r.wecom.how: In a WeCom group, add a group robot and copy its address. It can only send.
channel-setup.r.wecom.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.
channel-setup.r.whatsapp.field-phoneNumb: The phone number ID shown under WhatsApp, API Setup
channel-setup.r.whatsapp.how: Make a Meta app with the WhatsApp product, then copy the access token, the phone number ID and the app secret from its pages.
channel-setup.r.whatsapp.noCheck: Meta's read-only check needs the token inside the address, which Branch never does, so the token is checked when WhatsApp first posts to Branch.
channel-setup.r.whatsapp.pairing: Send a WhatsApp message to the business number. It answers with a six-digit code; approve it under Customize, Chat apps.
channel-setup.r.whatsapp.paste-WHATSAPP_: A word of your own choosing, typed into WhatsApp's webhook page too
channel-setup.r.x-dm.how: In the X developer portal, make an app with direct-message access and make a user access token for the bot's account. X charges for this API.
channel-setup.r.x-dm.noApp: X runs in the browser; the phone app is optional.
channel-setup.r.xmpp.noApp: XMPP is an open protocol with many programs (xmpp.org lists them); Branch connects by itself, so nothing needs installing.
channel-setup.r.xmpp.noCheck: There is nothing Branch can ask a web service to check; the connection is tried when the switch goes on.
channel-setup.r.xmpp.noCreate: XMPP accounts are made on the server you choose; there is no single sign-up page.
channel-setup.r.xmpp.step-1: Make an account for the assistant on an XMPP server.
channel-setup.r.zalo.how: Make an app on Zalo for Developers, link your Official Account, and copy the app secret, the OA secret key and the tokens.
channel-setup.r.zalo.noCheck: Zalo's check would spend the refresh token, so Branch leaves it for the first connection.
channel-setup.r.zulip.field-server: The address of your own server, starting with https://
channel-setup.r.zulip.how: Your Zulip opens on Personal settings, Bots. Add a new bot of the outgoing webhook kind and copy its API key.
channel-setup.r.zulip.noCheck: The only way to test an incoming address is to post a message into your chat, so Branch checks that it is an https address and leaves the first message to you.
channel-setup.safety: Only official apps and official pages are used. Branch never signs in as you and never drives BotFather or any app through your personal account.

channels-more.add-line: Add this to the channels list in the connections file, fill in the settings, and save the secrets it names in the default project:
channels-more.docs: How to set this up on their side
channels-more.intro: IRC, Mastodon, Bluesky, iMessage and more, each with its own switch. All of them start off: nothing connects until you switch it on and add it to the connections file.
channels-more.saved: Saved. Connected chat apps follow the new switches now.
channels-more.service.bluesky: Answers Bluesky direct messages sent to the assistant's account; needs its handle and an app password allowed to reach direct messages.
channels-more.service.deltachat: Chat with the assistant on Delta Chat, which carries messages over email; you need the deltachat-rpc-server program installed here with an account already set up.
channels-more.service.discourse: Answers private messages, mentions and replies on a Discourse forum; needs the forum address, the assistant's username and an API key.
channels-more.service.flock: Answers people who write to your Flock app's bot; you need the app secret and the bot token.
channels-more.service.gotify: Sends you a notification through your own Gotify server. Nobody can write back this way.
channels-more.service.guilded: Answers people who mention your Guilded bot in your server's channels; you need the bot's API token.
channels-more.service.homeassistant: Send notifications through a Home Assistant notify service; you need your Home Assistant address and a long-lived access token.
channels-more.service.imessage: Answers iMessages through the Messages app on this Mac. Branch needs Full Disk Access to read new messages and your permission to control Messages; nothing leaves Apple's own service.
channels-more.service.irc: Joins IRC channels under a nick of its own and answers when someone starts a line with that nick, or writes to it privately.
channels-more.service.keybase: Chat with the assistant on Keybase, one to one or in team channels; you need the Keybase app installed on this computer and signed in with the assistant's account.
channels-more.service.kook: Answers direct messages and channel mentions sent to your KOOK bot, and after a short break picks up what was missed; you need the bot's token from the KOOK developer site.
channels-more.service.mastodon: Answers mentions of the assistant's Mastodon account, privately when they wrote privately; needs the server address and an access token.
channels-more.service.mqtt: Lets devices and scripts on an MQTT broker send the assistant messages and receive its replies; you need the broker's address, the topics to use and, if asked, an account password.
channels-more.service.msteams-bot: Talks in Microsoft Teams as a proper bot, in one-to-one chats, group chats and channels; you need an Azure Bot registration with its app id and a client secret.
channels-more.service.mumble: Answers text messages on a Mumble server, privately or when named in a channel; you need the server's address, a username and, for a self-signed server, its certificate fingerprint.
channels-more.service.nextcloud-talk: Chat with the assistant in Nextcloud Talk conversations; you need your Nextcloud address, a user for the assistant with an app password, and the conversation tokens.
channels-more.service.nostr: Receive and answer encrypted Nostr direct messages through the relays you choose; you need a Nostr private key for the assistant saved as a secret.
channels-more.service.ntfy: Get notifications through ntfy, and optionally write to the assistant on a protected topic; you need the server address, a topic and, for writing back, an access token.
channels-more.service.pumble: Answers direct messages to your Pumble app's bot, and channel messages that mention it; you need the signing secret, the app key, the bot token and the bot's user id.
channels-more.service.pushover: Get notifications on your phone through Pushover; you need an application token and your user key.
channels-more.service.qq-bot: Answers people through an official QQ bot, in private chats, groups and guild channels; you need the bot's App ID and client secret from the QQ open platform.
channels-more.service.reddit: Answers Reddit private messages and username mentions through a script app on the assistant's account; needs the app's id and secret and the account password.
channels-more.service.revolt: Answers direct messages and mentions sent to your Revolt bot; you need the bot's token.
channels-more.service.simplex: Chat with the assistant privately on SimpleX Chat; you need the simplex-chat program running on this computer with its API switched on.
channels-more.service.sms: Text the assistant by SMS through Twilio; you need a Twilio number, the account SID and the auth token.
channels-more.service.synology-chat: Answers people who write to a Chatbot on your Synology NAS; you need the Chatbot's token and its incoming address.
channels-more.service.threema: Send Threema messages through a Threema Gateway ID in Basic mode; you need the Gateway ID, its secret and credits.
channels-more.service.twist: Answers in the Twist conversations you list; needs an access token for the assistant's Twist account and the conversation ids.
channels-more.service.twitch: Reads a Twitch channel's chat and answers when someone mentions the assistant's login. Needs a token from the Twitch developer console.
channels-more.service.vk: Answers messages sent to your VK community through its Long Poll API; you need the community's number and a community access token.
channels-more.service.webex: Answers people who write to your Webex bot, and in spaces when the bot is mentioned; you need the bot's access token and a webhook secret you choose.
channels-more.service.wechat-mp: Answers people who write to your WeChat Official Account, for 48 hours after they last wrote; you need a verified account, its AppID and AppSecret, and the safe-mode Token and EncodingAESKey.
channels-more.service.wecom-app: Answers colleagues who write to your company's own WeCom app; you need the CorpID, the app's AgentId and Secret, and the Token and EncodingAESKey from its message settings.
channels-more.service.x-dm: Answers X direct messages; needs your own X developer account on a paid API plan and a user access token.
channels-more.service.xmpp: Chat with the assistant from any XMPP (Jabber) app, one to one or in group rooms; you need an XMPP account for the assistant and its password.
channels-more.service.zalo: Answers people who message your Zalo Official Account; you need the app id, the app secret, the OA secret key and an access token with its refresh token.
channels-more.switch-note: Off never connects. When needed connects only when there is something to send, and lets go after fifteen quiet minutes. On stays connected.

channels-more.unavailable: This one cannot be reached from this computer.
channels.address.old-accepted: Addresses without that word on the end still work, so you have time to change them over.
channels.address.old-accepted-until: Addresses without that word on the end still work until {date}, so you have time to change them over.
channels.address.old-cost: What that costs: the old address is one anybody can find by guessing the name you gave this connection. A post that arrives at it and cannot prove itself is turned away with the same answer for every name, so nobody learns which services you use — but the door is there. Switch this off once every service has its new address. Whatever this says, Branch refuses the old shape outright whenever it is listening beyond this computer.
channels.address.turned-away: Posts to this address are being turned away for the next {minutes} minute(s). Something kept posting here with the wrong address — most often this service itself, still using an address you have since replaced. Copy the address above into the service's own settings. Your other connections are not affected: each one is counted on its own, and a post carrying the right address is never made to wait.
channels.address.turned-away-signature: This service reached the right address but could not prove the posts came from it, so it is being counted for the next {minutes} minute(s). Check that the shared secret in the service's own settings matches the one in your connections file. Nothing is being held back on the way in by this.
channels.address.turned-away-was: Posts to this address were being turned away recently. Something kept posting here with the wrong address — most often this service itself, still using an address you have since replaced. If messages went missing, copy the address above into the service's own settings.

comfort.note.autoUpdate: Install also waits until no task is working, checks the download, tries the new version on a copy of your work and keeps a safety copy first.
comfort.note.blockUploads: On: the browser refuses every file upload.
comfort.note.caName: A name you will recognise, such as Office proxy.
comfort.note.caPem: Paste one certificate authority's certificate. It is added to the ones this computer trusts; checks are never turned off.
comfort.note.confirmSensitive: On: every time the browser types, presses, sends a file or borrows your browser, it asks you first, whatever you allowed before.
comfort.note.dialogs: Dismiss presses Cancel, as always. Accept presses OK, which may confirm what the site asked.
comfort.note.extraIgnoreFiles: Names of files in the workspace's top folder, such as .aiignore, one per line. Their lines are added.
comfort.note.focusPrompt: Puts the cursor in the message box. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.lookInside: Opens Look inside for the newest task in this conversation: every step it took. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.maxRecordingSeconds: A recording stops by itself after this long. Empty: it runs until you let go, as always.
comfort.note.method: Your computer: a notification as well as the banner. This window only: just the banner.
comfort.note.newConversation: Starts a new conversation. Backspace leaves it with no keys.
comfort.note.newTrunk: Opens a new Trunk, an assistant of your own with its own name, face and conversation. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.noProxy: Host names, one per line, that are reached directly.
comfort.note.palette: Opens the box that finds pages, conversations and commands. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.searchHistory: Opens the search of your earlier conversations with the cursor in it. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.proxy: Such as http://proxy.example.com:8080. No user name or password. Empty: no proxy. Every address is still checked against what can reach out.
comfort.note.pushToTalkKey: Hold these keys to speak, as if holding Talk. Click here and press them; Backspace leaves none.
comfort.note.respectGitignore: On, as always: when there is no .branchignore, searches skip what .gitignore lists. Off: only .branchignore counts.
comfort.note.stopTask: Stops the task that is working in this conversation, as its Stop button does. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.sideList: Hides or shows the conversation list on the left. Click here and press the keys you want.
comfort.note.sidePane: Folds the side pane away and back, where there is room for it.
comfort.note.sound: A short sound when Branch needs you. Off makes no sound, as always.

comfort.note.statusLine: As always keeps today's line. Your choice shows the ticked pieces, in this order, in the window and the terminal.

describe.acorn: Shows or hides the turning acorn. It is only a picture.
describe.delight-style: How the acorn and the pet are drawn: in pixels, as they have always been, or in 3D. 3D falls back to pixels where this computer cannot draw it.
describe.delight-pet-on: Shows a small pet beside the acorn in the side list. Off, there is no pet and nothing of it runs.
describe.delight-pet-name: What your pet is called, up to 20 letters. It only shows in its name and its menu.
describe.delight-pet-talks: The pet says what Branch is doing in one small bubble at a time. Off, it stays quiet.
describe.delight-pet-tips: Now and then a short tip about what is on screen, each only once, and fewer as your rank rises. Off, no tips.
describe.delight-ach-on: Counts achievements from what really happens on this computer, only for you, never sent anywhere. Off, nothing is counted or written down.
describe.delight-ach-quiet: Earn achievements without any note or card popping up. They still show in the list.
describe.delight-bg-on: Shows your own picture, video, animation or 3D object behind the glass instead of the oak. Switching it off forgets the file.
describe.delight-bg-file: The file stays in this window on this computer and is never sent anywhere. Files that are too big are refused.
describe.delight-bg-scrim: How strongly the theme's own colour covers the background. More keeps text easier to read.
describe.delight-bg-fit: Whether the background fills the window, shows all of itself, or repeats.
describe.adapt-mode: Whether Branch may get what a stopped task is missing. Off: it only names it. When needed: it offers a fix when something really stopped. On: it also says so before you ask. It never fetches or installs anything until you say yes.
describe.admin-hours: How long a sign-in lasts before the person has to sign in again. Shorter is safer.
describe.advisor-ceiling: The check stops once it has used this much on one task.
describe.advisor-on: A second model reads each finished answer and says if something looks wrong. It costs a little more per task.
describe.analytics: Counts how Branch is used, only with your consent and only to a place you choose.
describe.approval-kind: One choice for every tool of this kind: ask you, refuse, or allow. It replaces the choices for those tools one by one.
describe.browser-enabled: Lets that task use your own browser, where you are signed in. Untick it to take it back.
describe.browser-name: A short name for the website you stay signed in to.
describe.browser-port: The door number your own browser opened for Branch. Only this computer can use it.
describe.browser-refused: Websites Branch must never open in your browser, one per line.
describe.browser-run: The task that may use your browser. Empty means the next one.
describe.browser-url: The page where you sign in to that website.
describe.chain-oidc: A person must also sign in through an identity service you linked.
describe.chain-passkey: A person must also confirm with a passkey on their device.
describe.chain-pin: A person must type their PIN to sign in. Untick it and the PIN is no longer asked.
describe.code-editor: Whether the code editor can open and save files in your workspace.
describe.commands-mode: Whether the / commands work here and in chat apps. Off hides them everywhere.
describe.counters: Whether counts about tasks are sent to a place you chose. Off sends nothing.
describe.danger-confirm: Type Branch Agent, exactly, to switch the button on. It is there so a misclick cannot remove Branch.
describe.danger-keep: Keeps the folder with your conversations and settings, so only Branch itself and what it downloaded go. It starts ticked; untick it and everything goes.
describe.dbg-enabled: Lets Branch run the debuggers you listed. Nothing is installed.
describe.dbg-keep: Keeps a program being debugged running between tasks.
describe.dbg-list: One debugger per line: a short name and the program.
describe.debate-ceiling: A whole debate stops once it has used this much.
describe.debate-exchanges: How many times each side may reply in a debate. More is thorough but slower.
describe.desktop-cap: A task must stop and ask again after this many screen actions.
describe.desktop-enabled: Branch may look at your screen and use the keyboard and mouse. Turning it off stops that at once.
describe.engines-args: What that program is given, one item per line.
describe.engines-azure: The name of your Azure speech key in the locker. The key itself stays locked away.
describe.engines-deepgram: The name of your Deepgram key in the locker. The key itself stays locked away.
describe.engines-elevenlabs: The name of your ElevenLabs key in the locker. The key itself stays locked away.
describe.engines-listen: The service that writes out what you say.
describe.engines-program: A reading-aloud program on this computer, used instead of a service.
describe.engines-region: The Azure region your speech service is in, such as westeurope.
describe.engines-speak: The service that reads replies aloud.
describe.engines-voice: Which voice the service uses. Empty uses its usual one.
describe.event-loop: Watches whether Branch itself is keeping up, and says so when it falls behind.
describe.everything: Off, the window shows one question and one box, and everything else is under More. On, every tab, meter and switch shows all the time. Kept for you.
describe.file-agents: Whether AGENTS.md in the project folder is read. On: at the start of every task. When needed: when the work calls for it. Off: never.
describe.file-heartbeat: Whether HEARTBEAT.md is read when it wakes on a schedule. Off means it has nothing to check.
describe.file-identity: Whether IDENTITY.md, the name and manner you gave it, is read before each task.
describe.file-memory: Whether MEMORY.md, the notes you wrote for it, is read before each task.
describe.file-sop: Whether SOP.md, your standing steps, is read before each task.
describe.file-soul: Whether SOUL.md, its character, is read. When it is, it replaces the built-in character.
describe.file-tools: Whether TOOLS.md, your notes about the programs here, is read before each task.
describe.file-user: Whether USER.md, what it should know about you, is read before each task.
describe.firewall-address: An address to check against your network rules. Nothing is contacted.
describe.folder-trust: Whether a folder must be trusted before the files it carries are read. Off reads every folder.
describe.gemini-client: The client id from your own Google project, used to sign in to Gemini. It is not secret.
describe.gemini-model: Which Gemini model answers once you are signed in.
describe.goal: Lets a task keep working until a goal you set is met.
describe.group-browse: Members may have Branch use web pages for them.
describe.group-commands: Members may have Branch run commands on this computer.
describe.group-files: Members may have Branch write files.
describe.group-message: Members may have Branch send messages.
describe.group-name: A name for a group of people who share the same permissions.
describe.group-read: Members may have Branch look things up for them.
describe.group-settings: Members may change how Branch is set up. Give this one sparingly.
describe.group-spend: Members may have Branch spend money.
describe.health-probe: Also sends a tiny message to your default model to prove it answers. This costs a little.
describe.heartbeat-second: Another model reads the news first and it only reaches you if both agree it matters. This costs a little more.
describe.identity-instructions: Standing instructions read before every task, in every project.
describe.identity-name: What your assistant calls itself. It applies from the next message.
describe.image-model: The model that draws pictures when you ask for one.
describe.keep-audio: No recording ever leaves this computer; services that would need one refuse instead.
describe.keep-running: Closing the window leaves Branch working, so schedules and chat apps keep going. Turn it off and closing the window stops everything.
describe.keychain: Whether Branch may read the passwords you listed from the Keychain. Off reads none.
describe.keychain-account: The account, when two items share the same name.
describe.keychain-name: The short name a task uses to ask for this entry.
describe.keychain-note: A reminder of what the password is for.
describe.keychain-service: The item's name in the Keychain.
describe.kit-file-text: Saving replaces the whole file. Whether it is read at all is decided by its switch, on the card for that file.
describe.kit-import: Nothing changes when you choose a file. You see what it would change, and choose.
describe.kit-preset: Choosing one changes nothing yet. Press the button below to see what it would change.
describe.kit-reset: Choosing changes nothing yet. Press the button below to see each value before and after.
describe.language: The language of this window, on this computer only. Replies follow the language you write in.
describe.limit-requests: One conversation waits once it has asked this many questions in a minute.
describe.limit-sender-requests: One person messaging you is held back after this many questions in a minute.
describe.limit-sender-tokens: One person messaging you is held back for the hour after this much thinking.
describe.limit-tokens: One conversation stops for the hour once it has used this much thinking.
describe.link-email: Only a sign-in with exactly this address counts as that person.
describe.link-person: The person whose account at that service you are linking.
describe.link-provider: The identity service they will sign in with.
describe.live-dollars: A live voice conversation also ends once it has cost this much.
describe.live-minutes: A live voice conversation ends by itself after this long.
describe.live-record: Writes into the task's record how much sound was sent, not the sound itself.
describe.live-vad: The service decides when you have finished speaking. Off means you say when.
describe.local-ceiling: Below this cost, a simple task uses the free model here instead of the cloud.
describe.local-exe: A speech program already on this computer, for writing out recordings without the internet.
describe.local-hard: Long or fiddly tasks go to the cloud model, which is usually better at them.
describe.local-model: The model file or name that program uses.
describe.local-models: Whether models running on this computer can be used. Off leaves them installed but unused.
describe.local-private: A task that mentions personal details stays on this computer, even when the cloud would be better.
describe.local-routing: Branch picks between the model here and the cloud model for each task. Off always uses your default.
describe.loop-guard: Stops a task that keeps repeating the same step. Off lets it carry on.
describe.ls-enabled: Lets Branch use the language servers you listed to understand code. Nothing is installed.
describe.ls-keep: Keeps a language server running between tasks, which is faster but uses memory.
describe.ls-list: One language server per line: a short name, the program, and the kinds of file.
describe.media-folder: Where pictures and sound are saved, inside your workspace.
describe.model-profile: A named set of model choices. Picking one changes which model does what from the next task.
describe.models-active: The model every new conversation starts with. A conversation can still pick its own.
describe.models-cooldown: A model that failed is not tried again for this many seconds.
describe.models-fallback: If the default model fails, the ticked ones are tried in order.
describe.models-reasoning: How long a model thinks before it answers. Thorough is slower and costs more.
describe.motion: Stops things sliding and spinning. Nothing else changes.
describe.move-in: Whether Branch may look in other assistants' folders to bring things over. Off never looks.
describe.never-break: Keeps Branch running through crashes and updates, restarting it if it stops. Off leaves it stopped until you open it again.
describe.nodes: Lets Branch on your other computers be asked for help. Off keeps work on this one.
describe.os-sandbox: Puts programs Branch runs behind a wall that limits what they can read and reach. Off lets them do what you can.
describe.os-sandbox-hidden: More places programs behind the wall may not even read.
describe.os-sandbox-keys: Which site each saved key belongs to; a program gets a stand-in, never the key.
describe.os-sandbox-network: Where programs behind the wall may connect. Further down the list reaches more.
describe.people-admin: Lets other people sign in to Branch from their own device. Off turns every other sign-in away; your own is not affected.
describe.phone-switch: Lets your phone reach Branch on this computer once you pair it. Turn it off and paired phones can no longer connect.
describe.play-compare: A question to send to two models side by side. Both are charged.
describe.play-tool: A tool to try by hand. Your approval rules still apply.
describe.policy-preset: How much Branch does without asking. A stricter choice asks more often; a looser one asks less.
describe.project-active: The project new conversations belong to, with its folder, instructions and secrets. Changing it affects the next conversation, not ones already open.
describe.project-board: Keeps each project's flows and schedules on one board. Off hides the board; nothing on it is lost.
describe.project-folder: Work in this project stays inside this folder of your workspace. Leave it empty to use the whole workspace.
describe.project-id: A short name with no spaces, used in addresses and files. It cannot be changed once the project is saved.
describe.project-instructions: Read at the start of every task in this project, on top of your usual instructions.
describe.project-name: The name you see in lists. You can change it at any time.
describe.project-preset: The model this project's conversations start with. Empty uses your default model.
describe.provider-client: The id the service gave you for Branch. It is not secret.
describe.provider-id: A short name for this service, used only inside Branch.
describe.provider-issuer: The service's own address, which Branch checks every sign-in against.
describe.provider-label: The words on the sign-in button people see.
describe.provider-preset: Fills in the form for a well-known identity service. Nothing is saved until you add it.
describe.provider-secret: The name of the locker entry holding the service's secret. The secret itself stays in the locker.
describe.provider-voice: Uses your model service's voice, which sounds better but sends the words to that service.
describe.pull-requests: Whether Branch may turn a change into a pull request.
describe.quiet-news: When on, a scheduled check only interrupts you when it found something new.
describe.read-aloud: Every reply is read aloud as it arrives.
describe.remote-alias: The name of the other computer in your SSH settings.
describe.remote-label: The name you will see for that computer.
describe.remote-programs: The only programs Branch may run there.
describe.remote-root: Work on that computer stays inside this folder.
describe.reply-audio: When someone sends a voice note on a chat app, the answer is a voice note too.
describe.retention: Offers to delete old conversations. Nothing goes without your yes.
describe.retention-days: Conversations older than this are offered for deletion. 0 ignores age.
describe.retention-export: Hands you a saved copy before anything is deleted.
describe.retention-mb: Once everything together — the words and the files attached to them — is bigger than this, the oldest are offered. 0 ignores size.
describe.reviewer-ceiling: One look stops once it has used this much.
describe.reviewer-connection: Which connection does the second look.
describe.reviewer-mode: A second model looks at a step before you are asked about it. Off means you are asked straight away.
describe.reviewer-rules: Your own rules for the second look, in plain words.
describe.round-limit: One conversation waits once it has asked the model this many times in a minute. 0 means no limit.
describe.rules-decision: What happens when the rule matches: ask you, refuse, or allow.
describe.rules-kind: What kind of thing the rule looks at.
describe.rules-pattern: Which folder, site, account or command. Empty means all of them.
describe.rules-tool: The tool this rule is about, or * for every tool.
describe.runtimes: Lets agents such as Claude Code or Codex answer a conversation you hand them. Off keeps every answer with Branch.
describe.sandbox-distro: Which Linux scripts run in, when they run on the Linux side.
describe.sandbox-image: The container scripts run in, when they run in a container.
describe.sandbox-windows: Scripts may run in Windows' throwaway desktop, which is wiped afterwards.
describe.screen-switch: Whether the screen and keyboard tools are offered at all. Off hides them.
describe.sdk-kit: Whether the tools for building your own app on Branch are offered.
describe.secret-name: The name programs use to ask for it, such as GITHUB_TOKEN.
describe.secret-project: The project the secret belongs to. Other projects cannot use it.
describe.secret-value: The secret itself. It is locked away on this computer and never shown again.
describe.security-audit: Checks Branch's own setup for weak spots by itself. It only reads.
describe.security-malware: Checks add-ons for known malware before they are used.
describe.share-relation: Whether they can only read it or also add to it.

Name the app and the person for it to do anything: a line written with * for either keeps the tick and no more. Be sure before you turn it on: a chat app cannot prove who is typing, so anyone who gets into that chat account, or who manages to pass themselves off as it, can approve those changes from their own phone. settings.dictation.intro: Speak, and the words appear in the message box as you say them, on this computer, for nothing, and nothing is sent anywhere. It uses a streaming speech program you installed yourself — Branch installs none of its own and downloads none — so where this computer has none, the line below says which one to install and the switch stays off. Dictation fills the message box; it does not send it. You press send, exactly as if you had typed. Nothing is written to disk, nothing is kept beyond the phrase being written out, and the words go to the screen rather than into any record. Words appear about a second behind you and may change as it hears more. Dictation is the owner's: nobody else who uses this computer is offered it.
settings.dictation.mode-note: Off, the Dictate control is not there and nothing can open the microphone. When needed, it appears once a conversation is open on screen. On, it is always there. That is the whole difference: which windows offer the control. On does not mean the microphone is open — no setting here ever opens one: only pressing Dictate does, and only at this window. Lockdown switches it off whatever this says.

settings.dictation.silence-note: Nobody speaking for this long ends the phrase and lets go of the microphone. Branch does not hold a microphone open for a room that has gone quiet.
settings.dictation.warning: Read this before you switch it on: while dictation is listening, the microphone stays open. A recording program runs for as long as you are dictating, which is what lets the words appear as you speak. This is the one place Branch holds a microphone open — the word that starts a turn takes one window of sound at a time and lets go of the microphone every window; this does not. It is opened when you press Dictate and closed the moment you press it again, a quiet room ends the phrase, the conversation closes, Branch is locked, or Lockdown comes on. The line below is on for exactly as long as the microphone is.

settings.wake-word.intro: Say your own word and Branch starts a turn, instead of holding the Talk button. Listening happens on this computer only: no sound ever leaves it, no file is written, and nothing is recorded or kept before your word has been heard — one window of sound is held, asked about, and dropped. Not every computer can listen: the line below says what this one really does, and whether it is listening this moment. While the switch is off, nothing listens at all and the microphone is let go of. Holding Talk stays the ordinary way in, and the word gives nothing away — the turn it starts is asked about exactly as the same words typed into the box would be, with the same questions. It carries only the one window your word was in, a second or two: nothing said after that window is heard, because no further sound is recorded. On Windows the engine listens for that one phrase alone, so there the turn carries just your word and nothing else.

settings.wake-word.word-note: Two or three syllables work best, and something you would not say by accident. With no word chosen there is nothing to listen for, so nothing listens.

linux-desktop.purpose: A throwaway Linux desktop in a container, which Branch can work in while you watch or take it over. It never touches this computer's own screen, and it is off until you switch it on.
linux-desktop.note: Nothing is ever downloaded: the image has to be on this computer already. While the desktop runs, a notice with a Take over button sits on top of everything. Once you take over, Branch cannot act in it, stop it or start another until you hand it back here. Switching this off takes the desktop down at once.
linux-desktop.state.yours: You hold the shared desktop. Branch cannot act in it until you hand it back.
linux-desktop.state.branch: Branch is using the shared desktop. You can take it over at any time.
linux-desktop.status.off: Switched off. Any shared desktop was taken down.
linux-desktop.status.taken-over: It is yours. Branch has let go of it.
linux-desktop.status.viewer-shown: Viewer connection info is shown above.
describe.linux-desktop-mode: Off: Branch cannot start a shared Linux desktop, and one that is running is taken down at once. When needed or on: Branch may start one in a container and work in it.
describe.linux-desktop-image: The container image a shared desktop starts from. It must already be on this computer; Branch never downloads it.

updates.provenance.notChecked: The build provenance record for this download was not checked: GitHub could not be reached, did not answer in time, or sent a record that could not be read. The update relies on the published checksum alone, which it passed.
